subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.
reasoning:
I'm uncertain about some of the exact API signatures like sweep options, so I'll lean on safer, more conservative constructs like primitives through the part builder rather than guessing at risky methods.

I'm designing the creature structure with a root "mantle" joint, a scaled head sphere, and eight arms built as chains of joints with tapered cylinder segments curling outward in a computed curve.

For suckers, I'm planning small spheres offset toward the underside of each arm segment, keeping the geometry simple while letting the arms curl toward the floor using an angle that drifts with distance from the body.

Now I'm giving one arm a lifted path so it rises up to hold a brass key, built from a torus bow, cylinder shaft, and box teeth. I'm also tapering the arm radius outward and placing the head sphere and elongated mantle bulb above the body, making sure everything sits above floor level.

I'm scattering small coral and rust-colored bumps across the upper hemisphere of the head for texture, plus flattened paler spots for mottling, computing their positions directly on the ellipsoid surface. For the eyes, I'm placing golden spheres with thin black pupil bars near the front sides of the head, topped with tilted rust-colored brow boxes to give the octopus a grumpy expression.

Working through pupil bar orientation...

Now I'm placing the eye positions relative to outward offsets and sketching the head geometry: an ellipsoid head centered around (0, 0.42, 0.02) and a mantle bulb behind it, defining their respective radii.

Working out eyeball and pupil placement using the outward direction vectors, then sketching a brow shape as a thin cylinder oriented along the tangent of the eye curve.

Now I'm placing a small key held at the arm tip, pointing upward with a brass shaft, a torus bow at top, and teeth boxes near the base.

For joints, I'm sticking with manual joint definitions rather than risking undocumented chain/role helpers, naming each arm joint explicitly and using a bone reference where needed.

Writing segment helper and color palette...

Checking that underside suckers sink negligibly into the floor so they stay hidden, while arms curling upward keep their suckers visible. I'm computing each arm's point path with increasing radius and quadratic curl angle per segment so tips lift naturally.

Writing path math...

Still placing body parts and setting up the joint hierarchy -- head, arms, eyes, and bumps all parenting under the body root. Now I'm sketching a vector helper and planning the part structure to support directional arrays before writing the final code.
